verses.1: He was forty-one years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jirmeya from Libnah.
verses.2: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Yehoyakim had done.
verses.3: For in the sight of Jehovah, Jerusalem and Judah would remain under his rule until he threw them down from his face. Then Zadokiah rebelled against King Babylon.
verses.4: In the ninth year of his reign, in the fifteenth month, on the twentieth day of that month, came Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. All his army also arrived at Jerusalem. They camped there and built a wall around it.
verses.5: And the city entered the fortress for twelve years, during the reign of King Zedekiah.
verses.6: On the fourth day of the seventh month, the famine in the city became worse. There was no bread for the people of that land.
verses.7: The city was destroyed, and all the soldiers fled from it. They left the city during the night, through a gate between two walls that were located on the king’s garden. Then, the enemies surrounded the city, and they continued their journey along the streets of the city.
verses.8: And the army of predators pursued the king. They captured Zedekiah in the middle of the night. All of his soldiers were killed.
verses.9: And they brought the king before King Babylon, Rebelatha, in the land of Hamath. They discussed matters with him.
verses.10: And the king of Babylon slaughtered all the sons of Zadok’s house, as well as all the priests of Judah. He also slaughtered them in Babylon.
verses.11: And the eyes of Jezreel were blinded, and they were prohibited from seeing. They were taken to Babylon by King Babel. There, they were kept in the prison until their death.
verses.12: And in the fifth month, twenty years after the beginning of the month, it was the age of seventy-and-twelve years for King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. Nebuzaradan, a high-ranking official, stood before King Babylon in Jerusalem.
verses.13: And he destroyed the Temple of God, as well as the king’s palace. He also burned down all the houses in Jerusalem, and every large building there.
verses.14: And all the inhabitants of Jerusalem were scattered around. Every army was destroyed by those fierce warriors.
verses.15: And the goods of the people, and all those who remained in the city, as well as those who were brought before King Babylon. Nebuzaradan, the high priest, took possession of all these goods.
verses.16: And from the fruits of the earth, Nebuzardan left behind many valuable things for the crops and for use in other purposes.
verses.17: And the poles of the candlesticks that are in the house of Jehovah, and also the vessels used for lighting the lamps, and the sea of candles that is also in the house of Jehovah – all these were broken apart by the dogs. And they carried all their candles into the abyss.
verses.18: And all those tools and instruments used for harvesting, such as sickles, scythes, and other devices used for gathering crops.
verses.19: And the vessels, and the containers, and the trays, and the utensils, and the basins, and the cups, and the bowls, all made of gold or silver. They were taken by those who were very rich.
verses.20: The two pillars that represent the two seas, and the twelve columns beneath them, which were made by King Solomon for the house of Jehovah, were not worth as much as all these other items.
verses.21: And the pillars were twelve cubits in height. The distance between each pillar was also twelve cubits. Their thickness was four cubits.
verses.22: And on it there was a seal. The time it took for the other seal to be made was five hours. And around the seal, there were ropes and ropes of nails. All of these were used as decorations for the second seal.
verses.23: And there were seventy-six heights in total. Each of these heights had a height of one hundred cubits around it.
verses.24: And Reuben-Tabachim took Shariyah, the chief priest, and Tzfanya, the high priest, as well as the three guards who were responsible for guarding the ark.
verses.25: And from the city, he took one officer who was in charge of the soldiers. He also took seven men who were close to the king’s face. These men were found in the city. There was also a record keeper who kept track of the people of the land. Additionally, there were sixty men from the people of the land who were found within the city.
verses.26: And Nebuchadnezzar, the great king, took them and went with them to King Babylon, Rebelatha.
verses.27: And King Babylon killed them. They died in Babylon, in the land of Hamath. And Judah was destroyed from its land.
verses.28: This is the people who brought Nebuchadnezzar to power during the seventh year of the reign of Judah. They numbered three thousand, one hundred and thirty-three people.
verses.29: In the year of thirty, Nebuchadrezzar from Jerusalem died at the age of thirty-two.
verses.30: In the year three hundred and twenty, during the reign of Nebukadnezar, the Jews who were very powerful, with seven thousand four hundred and fifteen people each, totaling four thousand six hundred people.
verses.31: In the thirty-seventh year of the reign of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, King Babel took Jehoiachin’s head from his place. He was taken out of the palace.
verses.32: And Tovot spoke to him, and he placed his throne above the throne of the kings who were in Babylon.
verses.33: And he renewed his clothes from time to time. He ate bread before him every day, throughout his entire life.
verses.34: And he received a constant punishment from the king of Babylon, day after day, until his death. All the days of his life were filled with such punishment.
